label: Homestead / Main Residence
volunteer_identification_guide: Primary domestic residence of pastoral leaseholder or station manager; often multi-room, formal symmetrical or picturesque plan, formal joinery, fireplaces, and verandahs.

label: Overseers / Bookkeepers Cottage
volunteer_identification_guide: Secondary domestic dwelling of modest scale; typically 2-4 rooms, simple gable or hipped roof with front verandah, housing permanent staff.

label: Detached Kitchen / Cookhouse
volunteer_identification_guide: Freestanding building situated 5-15m to rear of homestead to reduce fire hazard and heat; features large open cooking hearth, chimney stack, bread oven, or colonial range.

label: Shearers Quarters
volunteer_identification_guide: Linear or barracks-style multi-room accommodation for seasonal shearers; regulated by Rural Workers Accommodation Acts from early 1900s requiring specific bunk space and ventilation.

label: Station Dining Hall & Cookhouse
volunteer_identification_guide: Large communal mess hall, galley kitchen, and pantry serving pastoral workforce during shearing seasons.

label: Laundry / Washhouse
volunteer_identification_guide: Small outbuilding often containing copper boiler set in brickwork, timber troughs, and drainage gully.

label: Privy / Earth Closet / Outhouse
volunteer_identification_guide: Small timber or CGI booth positioned away from house; earth closet (Moule patent box, post-1860) or pit toilet over deep cesspit deposit.

label: Woolshed (Shearing Shed)
volunteer_identification_guide: Central complex of the pastoral station; contains sweat pens, raised shearing board (blade or machine), wool press area, classing tables, wool room, and counting-out pens under skillion.

label: Shearing Board (Component)
volunteer_identification_guide: The specific raised timber platform where sheep are shorn; look for worn timber battens, shafting/bracket scars from overhead mechanical shearing gear (Wolseley post-1887).

label: Sweat Pens / Forcing Pens
volunteer_identification_guide: Internal holding pens floored with slatted timber grates allowing sheep droppings to fall into sub-floor void.

label: Stables & Harness / Tack Room
volunteer_identification_guide: Accommodates draught horses and hacks; cobble, brick or timber floor, feed mangers, stall partitions, saddle racks, harness pegs, and feed loft above.

label: Coach House / Buggy Shed
volunteer_identification_guide: Vehicle shed for horse-drawn buggies, drays, and wagons; wide double ledged doors, earthen or packed stone floor.

label: Dairy / Milking Shed
volunteer_identification_guide: Cool, insulated masonry, pise, or double-slab outbuilding with concrete or brick drainage floor for milk cooling, cream separation, and butter churning.

label: Meat House (Cool Meat Storage)
volunteer_identification_guide: Elevated or shaded vernacular structure with steep hipped or pyramidal roof, flywire or louvred ventilation walls, overhanging eaves, and overhead meathooks/rail.

label: Hay Shed / Implement Shed
volunteer_identification_guide: Large open-sided bush pole or heavy timber framed structure clad in CGI for protecting tractors, threshers, harvesters, wagons, and loose or baled fodder.

label: Stockyard / Drafting Crush / Race
volunteer_identification_guide: Network of heavy post-and-rail fences, gates, draft races, and wooden crushes for handling cattle and sheep.

label: Sheep Dip & Drying Pens
volunteer_identification_guide: In-ground brick, stone, or concrete swim plunge trough (10-20m long) with arsenic/pesticide footbath, entry crush, and concrete sloped drying pen draining back into vat.

label: Boundary Riders / Outstation Hut
volunteer_identification_guide: Isolated single-room vernacular bush hut (slab, bark, or CGI) located on remote run paddocks, equipped with open fireplace and bunk.

label: Blacksmith / Forge / Farriery
volunteer_identification_guide: Workshop with stone or brick forge, bellows mount, anvil base (tree stump), quenching tub, slag and metal scrap accumulations, repairing station tools and shoeing horses.

label: Carpentry & Maintenance Shop
volunteer_identification_guide: Timber workshop with workbenches, tool racks, timber storage racks for fencing and building repairs.

label: Boiler / Stationary Steam Engine House
volunteer_identification_guide: Brick or heavy timber frame building housing steam boiler, pump, or stationary diesel engine powering woolshed overhead driveshafting.

label: Brick Kiln / Clamp Working
volunteer_identification_guide: Remains of on-site brick burning clamps or updraft scove kilns; vitrified brick bats, charcoal, ash lenses, and reddish baked soil.

label: Well / Sunk Well Shaft
volunteer_identification_guide: Deep circular excavation lined with dry-stone, brick, or timber lagging; may retain windlass, hand pump, or bucket gear.

label: Underground Cistern / Water Tank
volunteer_identification_guide: Subsurface brick or stone dome-topped subterranean tank sealed with lime/sand mortar or hydraulic cement for catching roof rainwater; predates cheap corrugated iron tanks.

label: Overhead Galvanised CGI Tank & Stand
volunteer_identification_guide: Circular corrugated sheet iron tank on elevated timber or steel stump stand, patented in Australia c. 1857; feeds reticulated gravity pipes.

label: Square Rivetted Iron Ship Tank
volunteer_identification_guide: Wrought iron square cube tank (~400 gallon / 1.2m cube) with rivetted flanges; originally cargo ship water/ballast tanks, repurposed throughout rural Australia.

label: Earth Tank / Station Dam & Silt Trap
volunteer_identification_guide: Excavated earthen reservoir with catch banks, drains, and silt trap designed for watering livestock across open pasture.
